nodes.description: Contract owner address, initialized from msg.sender at deployment and used as the withdraw authorization guard and payout recipient.
Hardcoded keccak256 hash of the secret number stored on-chain (0x04994f...b829).
Public owner-only function that transfers the entire contract balance to the owner.
Public payable function: if keccak256(number) matches secretNumberHash and msg.value > this.balance, sends jackpot to the caller.
Caller-controlled address; used as owner during construction, as withdraw guard and as recipient of the jackpot.
External value transfer of this.balance to owner executed inside withdraw.
External value transfer of the jackpot to the caller executed inside guess.
uint8 guess parameter supplied by the caller to guess.
Weak guess/authorization check: the 8-bit secret space (256 values) can be brute-forced off-chain because the hash is public and the winner also takes the contract balance.
Unchecked arithmetic addition of the contract balance and msg.value (Solidity 0.4.x has no overflow protection).

edges.reason: owner state variable is initialized directly from msg.sender at deployment, so the deployer controls withdrawal rights.
withdraw is gated by require(msg.sender == owner); the caller identity decides whether the transfer executes.
withdraw unconditionally triggers an external value transfer of this.balance to owner.
The caller address msg.sender is the recipient of the jackpot transfer in guess, making the caller an external party receiving funds.
guess conditionally performs an external value transfer to msg.sender when the guard conditions hold.
guess consumes the caller-supplied uint8 number parameter.
The number parameter is hashed and used as the left operand of the guess comparison.
secretNumberHash is read as the right operand of the guess comparison.
guess evaluates keccak256(number) == secretNumberHash; passing this weak check is the only access condition for the jackpot.
Satisfying the brute-forceable hash check unlocks execution of the jackpot transfer.
guess computes this.balance + msg.value without checked arithmetic.
The unchecked sum this.balance + msg.value flows into the payable transfer as the amount.
The owner address is the destination of the value transferred in withdraw.

normalization_plan.reason: The uint8 number parameter only exists to feed the guess function's hash check, so it is folded into the core guess function node.
